questions.question: Categorical propositions are most closely associated with which branch of philosophy?

options.A: Ethics

questions.question: Another name for categorical propositions is:

options.A: Hypothetical statements

questions.question: What branch of argumentation do categorical propositions fall under?

options.A: Inductive reasoning

questions.question: Which of the following is not a rule for a valid standard-form categorical proposition?

options.A: It must contain a subject and predicate.
options.D: It must be in the past tense.

questions.question: What does the quality of a categorical proposition indicate?

options.A: Whether it is about universal or particular cases
options.B: Whether the proposition is valid or invalid
options.C: Whether the statement is affirmative or negative
options.D: Whether the premises lead to a true conclusion

questions.question: What does the quantity of a categorical proposition refer to?

options.A: The level of certainty in the argument
options.B: Whether the statement applies to all or some members of a category
options.C: The number of premises needed for validity
options.D: The number of terms used in the argument

questions.question: A universal categorical proposition refers to:

options.A: A statement that applies to an entire category
options.B: A statement that applies to only some members of a category
options.C: A statement that is necessarily true
options.D: A statement that cannot be negated

questions.question: A particular categorical proposition refers to:

options.A: A statement that applies to an entire category
options.B: A statement that applies to only some members of a category
options.C: A statement that can never be false
options.D: A statement that is always valid

questions.question: Which categorical proposition is Universal Affirmative?

options.A: A

questions.question: Which categorical proposition is Universal Negative?

options.A: A

questions.question: Which categorical proposition is Particular Affirmative?

options.A: A

questions.question: Which categorical proposition is Particular Negative?

options.A: A

questions.question: What can be said about the truth value of a categorical proposition?

options.A: It can be true or false.
options.B: It can be valid or invalid.
options.C: It can be strong or weak.
options.D: It can be sound or unsound.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a cogent statement?

options.A: A statement that is both valid and sound
options.B: A statement with true premises but a false conclusion
options.C: A strong inductive argument with true premises
options.D: A deductive argument with a false conclusion

questions.question: What makes an argument weak?

options.A: The premises do not provide strong support for the conclusion.

questions.question: What makes an argument strong?

options.A: The conclusion follows with high probability from the premises.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes contradiction in categorical propositions?

options.A: Two statements that cannot both be true or false at the same time.
options.B: Two statements that can both be true but cannot both be false.
options.C: Two statements where one is universal, and one is particular.
options.D: Two statements that have no relation to each other.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes contrary opposition?

options.A: Two statements that can both be false but cannot both be true.
options.B: Two statements that must always be true.
options.C: Two statements that must always be false.
options.D: Two statements that have no logical relation.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes subalternation in categorical logic?

options.A: The truth of a universal statement guarantees the truth of a particular statement.
options.B: The falsity of a universal statement guarantees the truth of a particular statement.
options.C: The truth of a particular statement guarantees the truth of a universal statement.
options.D: The truth of one statement negates the other.

questions.question: Which of the following describes immediate inference?

options.A: A conclusion derived directly from a single premise.
options.B: A conclusion derived from multiple premises.
options.C: A conclusion that is always valid.
options.D: A conclusion that requires additional assumptions.

questions.question: When a statement can be false, and its opposite statement can also be false, their opposition is called:

options.A: Contradiction

questions.question: When a statement can be true, and its opposite statement must be false, their opposition is called:

options.A: Contradiction

questions.question: When a universal statement is true, and its particular counterpart must also be true, their opposition is called:

options.A: Contradiction

questions.question: When two statements can both be true but cannot both be false, their opposition is called:

options.A: Contradiction

questions.question: When a universal statement is false, and its particular counterpart may or may not be false, their opposition is called:

options.A: Contradiction
